pairs: Hæ quoque parabolæ Salomonis,
These, too, are parables of Solomon,
quas transtulerunt viri Ezechiæ regis Juda.
which the men of Hezekiah, king of Judah, transferred.
Gloria Dei est celare verbum,
It is to the glory of God to conceal a word,
et gloria regum investigare sermonem.
and it is to the glory of kings to investigate speech.
Cælum sursum,
Heaven above,
et terra deorsum,
and earth below,
et cor regum inscrutabile.
and the heart of kings are each unsearchable.
Aufer rubiginem de argento,
Take away the tarnish from silver,
et egredietur vas purissimum.
and a most pure vessel will go forth.
Aufer impietatem de vultu regis,
Take away impiety from the face of the king,
et firmabitur justitia thronus ejus.
and his throne shall be made firm by justice.
Ne gloriosus appareas coram rege,
Do not appear glorious before the king,
et in loco magnorum ne steteris.
and do not stand in the place of the great.
Melius est enim ut dicatur tibi:
For it is better that it should be said to you,
Ascende huc,
“Ascend to here,”
quam ut humilieris coram principe.
than that you should be humbled before the prince.
Quæ viderunt oculi tui ne proferas in jurgio cito,
The things that your eyes have seen, do not offer hastily in a quarrel,
ne postea emendare non possis,
lest afterward you may not be able to make amends,
cum dehonestaveris amicum tuum.
when you have dishonored your friend.
Causam tuam tracta cum amico tuo,
Argue your case with your friend,
et secretum extraneo ne reveles:
and do not reveal the secret to an outsider,
ne forte insultet tibi cum audierit,
lest perhaps he may insult you,
et exprobrare non cesset.
when he has heard it,
Gratia
and he might not cease to reproach you.
et amicitia liberant:
Grace and friendship free a man;
quas tibi serva,
preserve these for yourself,
ne exprobrabilis fias.
lest you fall under reproach.
Mala aurea in lectis argenteis, qui loquitur verbum in tempore suo.
Whoever speaks a word at an opportune time is like apples of gold on beds of silver.
Inauris aurea, et margaritum fulgens, qui arguit sapientem et aurem obedientem.
Whoever reproves the wise and obedient ear is like an earring of gold with a shining pearl.
Sicut frigus nivis in die messis,
Just like the cold of snow in a time of harvest,
ita legatus fidelis ei qui misit eum:
so also is a faithful messenger to him who sent him:
animam ipsius requiescere facit.
he causes his soul to rest.
Nubes,
A man who boasts
et ventus,
and does not fulfill his promises is like clouds
et pluviæ non sequentes,
and wind,
vir gloriosus et promissa non complens.
when rain does not follow.
Patientia lenietur princeps,
By patience, a leader shall be appeased,
et lingua mollis confringet duritiam.
and a soft tongue shall break hardness.
Mel invenisti: comede quod sufficit tibi,
You have discovered honey; eat what is sufficient for you,
ne forte satiatus evomas illud.
lest perhaps, being filled up, you may vomit it.
Subtrahe pedem tuum de domo proximi tui,
Withdraw your feet from the house of your neighbor, lest,
nequando satiatus oderit te.
when he has had his fill, he may hate you.
Jaculum, et gladius, et sagitta acuta, homo qui loquitur contra proximum suum falsum testimonium.
A man who speaks false testimony against his neighbor is like a dart and a sword and a sharp arrow.
Dens putridus, et pes lassus, qui sperat super infideli in die angustiæ,
Whoever sets his hopes on the unfaithful in a day of anguish is like a rotten tooth and weary foot,
et amittit pallium in die frigoris.
and like one who loosens his garment in cold weather.
Acetum in nitro, qui cantat carmina cordi pessimo.
Whoever sings verses to a wicked heart is like vinegar on baking soda.
Sicut tinea vestimento,
Just like a moth to a garment,
et vermis ligno,
and a worm to wood,
ita tristitia viri nocet cordi.
so too does the sadness of a man do harm to the heart.
Si esurierit inimicus tuus,
If your enemy is hungry,
ciba illum;
feed him.
si sitierit,
If he is thirsty,
da ei aquam bibere:
give him water to drink.
prunas enim congregabis super caput ejus,
For you will gather hot coals upon his head,
et Dominus reddet tibi.
and the Lord will repay you.
Ventus aquilo dissipat pluvias,
The north wind brings forth the rain,
et facies tristis linguam detrahentem.
and a sorrowful face brings forth a detracting tongue.
Melius est sedere in angulo domatis quam cum muliere litigiosa
It is better to sit in a corner of the attic,
et in domo communi.
than with an argumentative woman and in a shared house.
Aqua frigida animæ sitienti,
Like cold water to a thirsty soul,
et nuntius bonus de terra longinqua.
so too are good reports from a far away land.
Fons turbatus pede et vena corrupta,
The just falling down before the impious is like a fountain stirred up by feet
justus cadens coram impio.
and like a corrupted spring.
Sicut qui mel multum comedit non est ei bonum,
Just as whoever eats too much honey, it is not good for him,
sic qui scrutator est majestatis opprimetur a gloria.
so also whoever is an investigator of what is majestic will be overwhelmed by glory.
Sicut urbs patens et absque murorum ambitu,
Just like a city lying in the open and without surrounding walls,
ita vir qui non potest in loquendo cohibere spiritum suum.
so also is a man who is unable to restrain his own spirit in speaking.
